questions.question: Implement a Promise from scratch in JavaScript.
questions.title: Implement a Promise from Scratch — A+ Spec Explained
questions.direct_answer:
Implement a Promise from scratch in JavaScript.

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the type checker, emit pipeline, and how types line up with runtime JS), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** State machine (pending/fulfilled/rejected), then/resolve/reject, chaining via returning a new Promise, microtask scheduling.

**Classic weak answer:** Calling onFulfilled synchronously — per the A+ spec, callbacks must be run asynchronously (use queueMicrotask).

**Senior finish:** Reference the Promises/A+ spec, show then-chaining, add static resolve/reject/all/race, and mention the unhandled-rejection timer.

interviewer_intent.testing: State machine (pending/fulfilled/rejected), then/resolve/reject, chaining via returning a new Promise, microtask scheduling
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Calling onFulfilled synchronously — per the A+ spec, callbacks must be run asynchronously (use queueMicrotask)
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Reference the Promises/A+ spec, show then-chaining, add static resolve/reject/all/race, and mention the unhandled-rejection timer

sections.title: Why this question matters
sections.content:
This question — **Implement a Promise from Scratch — A+ Spec Explained** — shows up constantly in **frontend / fullstack** interviews because it separates candidates who memorized docs from candidates who can **reason about real systems**.

**Restate the prompt:** Implement a Promise from scratch in JavaScript.

A gold-level answer does four things in order:

1. **Define** the terms in plain English (what it is / what problem it solves).
2. **Explain the mechanism** (what runs when: browser, bundler, framework, network).
3. **Compare trade-offs** (speed vs correctness vs security vs DX) with **when you would not use** the default.
4. **Ground it in production** — caching, auth, observability, tests, or an incident you handled.

Interviewers are listening for: **State machine (pending/fulfilled/rejected), then/resolve/reject, chaining via returning a new Promise, microtask scheduling**.

The fastest way to lose points is: **Calling onFulfilled synchronously — per the A+ spec, callbacks must be run asynchronously (use queueMicrotask)**.

If you only add one “senior” layer, make it: **Reference the Promises/A+ spec, show then-chaining, add static resolve/reject/all/race, and mention the unhandled-rejection timer**.

sections.title: Deep dive — what to say
sections.content:
### What to explain (middle of the answer)

- **Core mechanics:** State machine (pending/fulfilled/rejected), then/resolve/reject, chaining via returning a new Promise, microtask scheduling
- **Concrete shape:** give a small code or config snippet *only if it clarifies* (5–15 lines max).
- **Interviewer follow-ups:** expect “what breaks in production?”, “how do you debug?”, “what would you measure?” — answer them proactively.

### How to sound senior (without rambling)

- Tie the feature to **user-visible outcomes** (performance, accessibility, security).
- Mention **one failure mode** you have actually seen (race, stale cache, hydration mismatch, flaky test).
- Close with **one decision rule** (“choose X when …; choose Y when …”).

sections.title: Trade-offs & senior signal
sections.content:
### Trade-offs interviewers expect you to name

- **Speed vs safety** (types, runtime checks, validation).
- **DX vs constraints** (framework magic vs explicit wiring).
- **SEO / first paint vs interactivity** (SSR/SSG/CSR choices where relevant).
- **Security vs convenience** (tokens, cookies, localStorage, third-party scripts).

### What “book answer” misses

- **Book answer:** repeats definitions.
- **Strong answer:** names **calling onFulfilled synchronously — per the A+ spec, callbacks must be run asynchronously (use queueMicrotask)** and what you do instead.

**Body (45–60 seconds):** Walk through **State machine (pending/fulfilled/rejected), then/resolve/reject, chaining via returning a new Promise, microtask scheduling** as a story: what runs, what breaks, what you log/measure.

**Pitfall (15 seconds):** Call out **Calling onFulfilled synchronously — per the A+ spec, callbacks must be run asynchronously (use queueMicrotask)** — interviewers reward honesty about real bugs.

questions.question: Implement an EventEmitter / Pub-Sub system in JavaScript.
questions.title: Implement EventEmitter in JavaScript — Pub/Sub from Scratch
questions.direct_answer:
Implement an EventEmitter / Pub-Sub system in JavaScript.

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the type checker, emit pipeline, and how types line up with runtime JS), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** Map of event -> listeners, on/off/once/emit API, error handling, memory-leak prevention (limit listeners, remove on unmount).

**Classic weak answer:** Not returning an unsubscribe function from on() — callers then can't reliably remove anonymous listeners.

**Senior finish:** Show once implementation via wrapped callback; add a return unsubscribe function to on(); note RxJS Subject as the reactive equivalent.

interviewer_intent.testing: Map of event -> listeners, on/off/once/emit API, error handling, memory-leak prevention (limit listeners, remove on unmount)
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Not returning an unsubscribe function from on() — callers then can't reliably remove anonymous listeners
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Show once implementation via wrapped callback; add a return unsubscribe function to on(); note RxJS Subject as the reactive equivalent
